Scapula fractures: 4

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A displaced intra-articular glenoid fracture heals with persistent joint-surface incongruity. Over time the patient develops pain, restricted movement and degenerative changes. Which complication best explains the consequences of the residual articular mismatch?

  1. Acute compartment syndrome
  2. Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
  3. Joint stiffness
  4. Osteonecrosis
  5. Nonunion
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis

Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes.

Understanding the options

Post-traumatic osteoarthritis
Articular incongruity or cartilage damage can cause later degenerative joint changes.
Joint stiffness
Capsular contracture, adhesions and prolonged immobilization can restrict motion after injury. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Osteonecrosis
Disruption of blood supply can lead to death and collapse of an injured bony segment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Nonunion
Persistent failure of fracture healing requires assessment of stability, biology, infection and patient factors. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
Acute compartment syndrome
Rising compartment pressure impairs perfusion; escalating pain and pain on passive stretch require urgent assessment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
